# /crav1-host-setup

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [Set up a host setting](../../from-host-setup.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-host-setup/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Change one Azure DevOps or GitHub setting that does not live in the repo, through a checked-in script applied after a yes and read back live.

1.115.0: a host setting with no file in the repo (a branch policy or required build, required reviewers, an environment approval, a variable group) is built like code. You describe it; the kit drafts a checked-in `az` or `gh` script under `infra/ado/` or `infra/github/` with a what and why comment above each command, and generates the manual steps from those comments. You see the commands, their scope and the steps, reply with edits until it is right, then yes. It runs the script, reads the live setting back with the script's `check` part and commits the script on a work branch. Done means the read-back says `ok`. Service connections and secret values are always manual: the script only checks they exist by name. Pipeline YAML, templates and infrastructure as code stay ordinary code. The plan route (plan-from-spec, build-tasks, verify) uses the same shared reference for `(host setup)` tasks, so both routes write the same script.

## Runs when

You need a branch policy, required build, reviewers, an approval or a variable group set on the host. Called by the user. Plan tasks marked `(host setup)` follow its shared reference inside build-tasks.

## Prompts

Prompt budget: 3 (the most prompts in one run, the closing yes included). A prompt may hold several questions. See the asking rule in `crav1.mdc`.

## Reads

In short: The ask, the repo's remote and pipelines, and the live host setting.

Reads the ask, `docs/system/repos.md`, the git remote, the repo's pipeline YAML and, when signed in, the live host setting (`az` or `gh`).

## Writes

In short: After a yes, the host setting itself, and a checked-in script committed on a work branch.

After an explicit yes to the shown script, applies the setting on the host, runs the read-back, and commits the script (`infra/ado/<name>.sh` or `infra/github/<name>.sh`) on a work branch.

## Does not

Leaves secret values, specs, plans, pull requests and threads alone. Does not push.

Limits and exceptions: Not signed in, or a headless run, drafts and stops without applying. Something the host reads from the repo is code and is routed to its lane. A larger ask is offered as a spec.
